_comment: Regression gate for the deterministic CI tier. Update deliberately, in its own commit, with the evaluation report that justifies the new numbers. Raising a threshold to make a red build green is the exact failure mode this project exists to prevent.
_semantics: Every number in this file is a TARGET THRESHOLD chosen by a human, not a measurement. Measured values are never written here automatically.
_measured_values: reports/retrieval_baseline.json holds the measured Phase B retrieval baseline (10-case dataset v1). reports/golden_baseline.json holds the measured Phase D baseline (50-case dataset v2). Compare against them before changing any threshold below.
_retrieval_v2_provenance: The retrieval_v2 targets are regression floors set deliberately below the first measured v2 run (2026-08-15, reports/golden_baseline.json), not copies of it. Measured: hit_rate_at_1 0.8182, hit_rate_at_3 0.8864, hit_rate_at_5 1.0, recall_at_5 0.9621, recall_at_10 1.0, mrr_at_5 0.8784, keyword_recall 1.0, citation_id_validity 1.0. A floor exists to catch a fall, so it sits below the measurement on purpose; it must never be moved down to accommodate one.

_latency_targets_ms._note: Not ratios, so kept out of the scored sections. Retrieval only, model load excluded.

_unvalidated_note: The end_to_end and ragas thresholds have never been measured; no LLM tier has run. reranked_v2 is empty pending its first measured nightly run. Treat them as placeholders until a measured report exists. An empty section is not a passing gate: the test that reads it skips with instructions rather than reporting green.

retrieval.mean_top_confidence.reason: Wrong shape of gate, not merely a wrong number. It thresholded the MEAN of the top normalised reranker score, which cannot detect the failure it appeared to guard against. Before the Phase C double-sigmoid correction, sentence-transformers applied its own sigmoid inside predict() and the code applied a second one, collapsing every score to sigmoid(0.0007) = 0.5002. Discrimination was entirely gone, yet a 'mean >= 0.5' gate PASSED. A gate that a totally broken implementation satisfies is not a gate.
retrieval.mean_top_confidence.measured_after_correction: Phase C, reports/reranking_comparison.json, 10-case v1 dataset: top-1 normalised scores 0.0001, 0.0106, 0.0118, 0.4670, 0.7530, 0.7551, 0.7558, 0.8129, 0.9738, 0.9824. Mean 0.5523. The corrected implementation discriminates across nearly the full range; the collapsed one did not.
retrieval.mean_top_confidence.why_not_re_thresholded: It measures reranker score calibration, not retrieval quality, so it does not belong in a retrieval gate: swapping the reranker model moves it while retrieval is unchanged. It is also an absolute threshold on an uncalibrated logit-sigmoid. The deterministic Phase D gate no longer loads the reranker, so it cannot produce this number at all.
retrieval.mean_top_confidence.still_reported: evaluate_retrieval() still computes mean_top_confidence and oos_mean_top_confidence for observability. They are recorded, not gated, and remain useful evidence for the Phase F threshold work.

_dataset_version_note: The retrieval section targets were set against dataset v1 (10 cases) and are retained for historical comparison. The retrieval_v2 section targets the current v2 dataset (50 cases). Aggregates from the two datasets are not comparable.
_reranked_v2_note: Gate for the reranked retrieve-then-rerank path, read by the slow nightly test. Empty until a measured run exists. Populate only from a real run of that test's evaluator on dataset v2, with floors set below the measurement, exactly as retrieval_v2 was done. Do not copy retrieval_v2 here: those numbers were measured without the reranker and the reranked path returns 5 results rather than 20.
